Oxidization property of the cold-rolled foils was evaluated by the isothermal oxidization test in air at 1173K until 48 h, using a thermogravimetry–differential thermal analysis (TG-DTA).
For the Ni 3(Si,Ti) and Ni 3(Si,Ti)+Nb alloys with a L1 2 single-phase microstructure, the fracture surfaces at high temperature showed intergranular fracture (Fig.5a).

For the Ni 3(Si,Ti)+Cr and Ni 3(Si,Ti)+Cr,Nb alloys with a two-phase microstructure, the fracture surfaces were prevailed by ductile transgranular fracture patterns (i.e., dimple patterns) in all the temperature range investigated, as shown in Fig.5b.
Tensile (fracture) strength as well as yield strength of the cold-rolled foil is slightly higher in the Nb and/or Cr added Ni 3(Si,Ti) alloys than in the Ni 3(Si,Ti) alloy.
Therefore, the improved high-temperature elongation for the Ni 3(Si,Ti) alloy is assumed to be due to the two-phase microstructure, by which the intergranular fracture was prevented.
Therefore, the improved oxidization resistance observed in the Cr added Ni 3(Si,Ti) alloys is attributed to the formation of protective Cr 2 O3 layer.
On the other hand, for the Nb added Ni 3(Si,Ti) alloy, protective SiO 2 layer may be enhanced by addition of Nb or diffusion process during oxidization may be suppressed by Nb.
